title: Design a News Feed (Twitter/Instagram)
subtitle: From pull-on-read SQL queries to fan-out hybrid push/pull with Redis feed caches

stages.title: Stage 1 — Pull Model on Relational DB
stages.bottleneck: Heavy SQL JOINs across users, follows, and posts tables on every home feed refresh.
stages.narrative:
**Pull model (Fan-out on Read).** When a user opens their feed, the app queries the DB for all users they follow, pulls their recent posts, orders them by timestamp, and returns them.

**Problem:** At 1,000 followees per user, every feed request triggers expensive indexed disk reads.

stages.title: Stage 2 — Push Model with Redis Feed Caches
stages.bottleneck: Celebrity problem (Fan-out on Write). If a user with 50M followers posts, 50M Redis writes overload the system.

edges.label: LPUSH post_id into each follower timeline

stages.narrative:
**Push model (Fan-out on Write).** When a user posts, async workers push the `post_id` directly into every follower's Redis timeline cache.

**Advantage:** Feed generation is instantaneous (`O(1)` ZRANGE read).

**Flaw:** Writing to 50 million follower timelines for a celebrity post causes massive write amplification and delay.

stages.title: Stage 3 — Hybrid Fan-Out Architecture
stages.bottleneck: Storing entire post payloads in Redis consumes enormous RAM.
stages.narrative:
**Hybrid Model & ID-only Timelines.** Regular users use Push (Fan-out on Write). Celebrities (>10K followers) use Pull (Fan-out on Read).

**ID-only caching:** Timelines store only 64-bit `post_id`s in Redis. Content (text, media URLs, author info) is hydrated in a single multi-get batch call.

stages.title: Stage 4 — ML Ranking & Media CDN Delivery
stages.bottleneck: Chronological feeds lack engagement; serving heavy video/image assets directly from storage exhausts bandwidth.
stages.narrative: **Personalized Feed Ranking Engine.** Candidates are generated via vector similarity & social graph, then passed to lightweight GBDT / Neural Net ranking models that score posts based on click/like probability.
